title: How to Track Job Applications With Claude, ChatGPT and Other AI Assistants
summary: Gmail, Notion and Sheets connectors can turn Claude or ChatGPT into a job tracker. Here’s the 2026 setup, and how Tsenta logs every application it sends.
body_markdown:
**The best Claude connectors for tracking job applications are Gmail, which finds application confirmations and recruiter replies, and Notion, Google Sheets or Airtable, which hold the tracker itself.** Turn on Gmail and one tracker app, paste the prompt below, and Claude proposes each change for you to approve. ChatGPT, Meta Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct and OpenClaw can run the same setup with different gaps, and none of these trackers sends applications. If you want the log to fill itself as applications go out, use an agent that submits them and records each one, such as Tsenta, which connects to your assistant through its MCP server.


Below are a tracker template, a prompt and steps for each assistant, using connectors that the assistant’s maker or the app’s maker documents, plus two community skills we flag as such, then a comparison with Tsenta’s tracker.


Checked November 20, 2026, and prices are as of that date. Tsenta publishes this guide and sells the agent it compares. We read each maker’s docs but did not run every setup end to end, so follow the maker’s current steps if they differ.


## The setup at a glance: what each assistant connects to


Assistant Gmail Notion Google Sheets Airtable Runs without you asking Tsenta’s MCP server


**Claude** Directory, made by Google Directory, made by Notion Sheets connector edits live; Drive reads sheets Directory, made by Airtable Scheduled tasks on paid plans Documented, as a custom connector


**ChatGPT** Plugin directory Plugin directory Through the Google Drive app Plugin directory, made by Airtable Scheduled tasks; Gmail-triggered tasks on Plus and Pro Documented, as a custom plugin; full access on Business, Enterprise or Edu, read only on Pro


**Meta Muse** Named by Meta, as is Outlook Named by Meta Not named Not named Recurring tasks No documented setup yet


**Grok Bot** App in its docs App in its docs App in its docs Not in its docs Routines Possibly, as a custom connector; no Tsenta guide


**Instinct** Through Google Workspace Not on its public pages In its August 2026 privacy policy Not on its public pages Not documented No documented setup yet


**OpenClaw** Pub/Sub trigger with Google Cloud setup, or an IMAP trigger for allowlisted senders Notion’s MCP server, added by you Not documented Airtable’s MCP server, added by you Automations An MCP server rather than a skill; no Tsenta guide


“Not named” and “not documented” mean the maker’s public pages did not mention it. Meta says Muse’s full connector list is only in its settings.


## A simple job application tracker template


Build it as a Notion database, a Google Sheet or an Airtable table. Make **Status** a single-choice field with Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected and Ghosted, the five stages Tsenta’s tracker uses.


Column What goes in it Example


Company Employer name as on the posting Acme


Role Job title Backend Engineer


Job link The posting or application URL Link to the posting


Date applied YYYY-MM-DD 2026-11-18


Status One of the five stages Applied


Applied through Company site, LinkedIn, Indeed, referral or an agent Company site


Résumé version The file you sent backend-v3


Last contact Date of the latest email either way 2026-11-19


Next step and due date One action, one date Thank-you note by 2026-11-21


Notes Contact, pay range, interview round Phone screen booked


Company, Role, Job link, Date applied, Status and Notes match the fields Tsenta’s tracker records, so the sheet can move into Tsenta later with **Import CSV** .


### The copy-paste prompt


Replace the bracketed part. The prompt reads, proposes and waits, so nothing is written until you say yes.


```text
You keep my job application tracker up to date.


Tracker: [name of my Notion database, Google Sheet or Airtable table]
Columns: Company, Role, Job link, Date applied, Status, Applied through,
Résumé version, Last contact, Next step and due date, Notes.
Status is always one of: Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected, Ghosted.


1. Search my email from the last 7 days for application confirmations,
recruiter replies, interview invitations, assessments, offers and
rejections. Skip job alerts and newsletters.
2. Match each message to a row by company and role. If a confirmation
matches no row, propose a new row.
3. For each row, propose the new Status, Last contact and Next step.
Quote the sentence from the email that supports it.
4. Propose Ghosted for any Applied row with no contact in 21 days.
5. Show every proposed change in one table and wait for my yes before
you write anything.
6. Never send, reply to, delete, archive or label email. Never delete a row.


```


Run it by hand once before you schedule it, and check for wrong matches and duplicates.


## Claude connectors: Gmail plus Notion, Google Sheets or Airtable


Anthropic’s directory lists[Gmail](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/gmail) , made by Google,[Notion](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/notion) , made by Notion, and[Airtable](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/airtable) , made by Airtable, which can create and update records.[Anthropic’s Google Workspace guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10166901-use-google-workspace-connectors) adds a Google Sheets connector that edits a sheet live beside the chat. Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive are on every Claude plan; on Team and Enterprise an owner enables them first.


1. Open **Customize** , then **Connectors** , and connect Gmail plus Notion, Airtable or Google Sheets.
2. Set each connector’s write tools to **Always ask** if you see that option ([Claude’s connector docs](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/getting-started) ), or keep the chat in **Manual** mode.[In Auto mode](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork) , a tool set only to **Needs approval** can run without asking.
3. In a chat, open **+** , then **Connectors** , turn both on and paste the prompt.
4. On a paid plan, type` /schedule` in Cowork, or ask for “every weekday at 8 AM”, to make it a[scheduled task](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork) . A task that reaches a tool set to ask first may wait or finish without it, so let it draft the changes and approve them when you open the result.


Claude asks before it sends, replies to or forwards Gmail, except in Auto mode, where Anthropic says an automated check decides and can miss risky actions, so keep the prompt’s “never send” line.[Claude Pro](https://claude.com/pricing) is $20 a month billed monthly as of November 20, 2026,[Notion](https://www.notion.com/pricing) has a $0 Free plan, and[Airtable says](https://support.airtable.com/docs/using-the-airtable-mcp-server) its MCP server adds no charge to your plan.


To skip the prompt,[Dalia Abbruciati’s community skill](https://github.com/daliaabbruciati/job-application-tracker-SKILL) scans Gmail, checks Google Calendar for interviews and updates a Notion database. Anthropic did not make it, so read it before you upload it. More in our[best Claude connectors for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-claude-connectors-job-search-2026) .


## ChatGPT apps: Gmail, Google Drive, Notion and Airtable plugins


ChatGPT’s add-ons are now plugins, and the **Plugins** directory lists[Gmail](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/gmail) , Notion,[Airtable](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_693ca6ce2db08191bb52d66743c65184) , made by Airtable, which can create and update records, and Google Drive, which[covers Docs, Sheets and Slides](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10929079-google-drive-app-and-setup-in-chatgpt) . OpenAI says[availability](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connected-apps-in-chatgpt) depends on the app, plan, region, workspace and interface.


1. In **Plugins** , connect Gmail and one of Google Drive, Notion or Airtable.
2. Set each app to **Always ask** or **Allow read actions** ([OpenAI’s permissions guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001495-managing-app-permissions-in-chatgpt) ).
3. In a chat, type` @` to pick Gmail and your tracker app, then paste the prompt.
4. OpenAI’s[August 25, 2026 release note](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes) says Plus and Pro users can have ChatGPT Work respond when a new Gmail message arrives, pausing actions that need approval. Free users get up to three daily scheduled tasks, and Free and Go cannot create Gmail-triggered tasks.


Test Notion writes first: its listing advertises editing pages and databases, while[OpenAI’s Notion article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12532955-notion-app-and-setup-in-chatgpt) says writes depend on the app, your Notion permissions and workspace settings.


OpenAI’s own[Track job applications use case](https://learn.chatgpt.com/use-cases/track-job-applications) is labeled a Codex use case, to try in the ChatGPT desktop app. It builds a spreadsheet from your résumé, notes and job descriptions, with each role’s status, deadline and next action. It connects no email or tracker app, so you type every status change. For apps that apply, read our[best ChatGPT apps for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-chatgpt-apps-job-search-2026) , and for tracker GPTs before OpenAI retires custom GPTs on December 11, 2026, our[custom GPTs for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-custom-gpts-job-search-2026) .


## Meta Muse connectors: Gmail, Outlook and Notion


Meta Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent, not The Muse job board, and Meta lists it in the US, Canada, Singapore and[Australia](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/muse-is-now-available-in-australia/) . Meta names[Gmail and Outlook](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1149305437517250/) as inboxes you can connect and Notion among its[work connectors](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business) .


1. Say “Connect my Gmail”, or open **Settings** , then **Connectors** ([Meta’s connector guide](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1687253048996149/) ). Many connectors can be set to retrieve data only, which suits Gmail.
2. Connect Notion and name your tracker database, or ask Muse to build the tracker as a[Space](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/introducing-spaces-customize-muse-app/) , a custom view you describe.
3. Paste the prompt and ask Muse to repeat it; it can[run recurring tasks on a schedule](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1484325780075655/) .


By default, Muse asks before important actions such as sending an email. Meta’s pages do not name Google Sheets, Google Drive or Airtable. Muse is[free with a weekly usage limit](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/) , with Power at $20 a month and Maximum at $100 as of November 20, 2026. Because Muse is an agent that can[browse and act on websites](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2124746764949121/) , it can open tsenta.com and work in your Tsenta account in its browser, the way you would. That is ordinary browsing, not a Muse connector or integration. More in[Meta Muse and job applications](https://tsenta.com/blog/meta-muse-apply-to-jobs-2026) .


## Grok Bot plugins: Gmail, Google Sheets and Notion apps


[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) describe a Gmail app that can search, read, draft, send and label mail, one mailbox at a time. A Google Sheets app reads and edits cells, a Google Drive app finds the file, and Notion is listed too.


1. Open **Connect apps** , add Gmail plus Google Sheets and Google Drive, or Notion, and finish each sign-in within about 10 minutes.
2. In a chat, type` @` to attach the apps and paste the prompt.
3. Ask for “every weekday at 8:00 AM” to make it a[routine](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/skills-routines-and-automations) . A routine can also start when an email reaches your Bot’s own address.


Auto Review shows an approval card when an action needs your OK. Grok Bot’s docs do not name Airtable. Grok Bot comes with The X Subscription’s[Premium plan at $30 a month](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/pricing) or higher as of November 20, 2026, and the $8 Plus plan excludes it. More in our[best Grok Bot plugins for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-grok-bot-plugins-job-search-2026) .


## Instinct connectors: Google Workspace only


Instinct is a personal assistant you text or call.[Its privacy policy](https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) , revised November 17, 2026, names one connection, Google Workspace, giving “your calendar and email inbox” as examples. The[August 2026 version](https://web.archive.org/web/20261101075823/https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) also listed Drive, Docs and Sheets, so Gmail plus a Google Sheet is the closest fit.


1. Sign up with your phone number at app.instinct.com, or join the waitlist when it is at capacity.
2. Link Google Workspace in your Instinct workspace settings.
3. Text Instinct the prompt with your Google Sheet’s link and ask for a weekly summary. Its[terms](https://instinct.com/terms) say it may message you first but give no scheduling details, so check that the first run opens your sheet.


Instinct’s public pages do not mention Notion, Airtable, custom connectors or MCP servers. Its terms make you responsible for “meaningful human oversight over all Actions” and say it is currently free. See our[Instinct connectors guide](https://tsenta.com/blog/instinct-ai-connectors-job-search-2026) .


## OpenClaw skills: a tracker skill or Notion and Airtable servers


OpenClaw is a free, open-source assistant you run yourself, paying only for the AI model you connect.


**A tracker skill.**` openclaw skills install @mkpareek0315/job-hunt-tracker` installs[Job Hunt Tracker](https://clawhub.ai/mkpareek0315/skills/job-hunt-tracker) . It keeps applications, follow-ups and offers in JSON files under` ~/.openclaw/job-hunt-tracker/` and makes no network requests of its own, so its files stay on your computer, though the AI model you connect still sees what you tell it. It reads no email: you tell it each update.


**Notion or Airtable as an MCP server.**[Notion’s guide](https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/get-started-with-mcp) gives` https://mcp.notion.com/mcp` over Streamable HTTP, and[Airtable’s](https://support.airtable.com/docs/using-the-airtable-mcp-server) gives` https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp` with OAuth.[OpenClaw’s docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/mcp/transports) save a remote server with its transport and OAuth, then sign in:


```text
openclaw mcp set notion '{"url":"https://mcp.notion.com/mcp","transport":"streamable-http","auth":"oauth"}'
openclaw mcp login notion


```


Keep the transport field, because OpenClaw uses SSE without it. We built these commands from the makers’ docs and did not run them.


**Gmail.** OpenClaw’s Gmail trigger docs use[Pub/Sub](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/gmail) , with Google Cloud setup and a public HTTPS endpoint. Its[IMAP email trigger](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/imap) needs neither but acts only on senders you allowlist. OpenClaw documents no Google Sheets connector.[Automations](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs) run the prompt on a schedule. OpenClaw says to treat third-party skills as code you choose to trust. See our[best OpenClaw skills for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-openclaw-skills-job-search-2026) .


## The other way: an agent that logs every application it sends


Every setup above logs what your assistant can read. Tsenta starts from the other end: it sends the applications, so each one it submits enters its tracker automatically. Tsenta watches 300,000+ company career pages, ranks roles in your match feed, tailors your résumé in Honest or Aggressive mode, or sends it as written, and submits on supported company career sites. On Starter and Pro you choose each role; Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles without per-role approval, needs Power.


**What the tracker holds.** Company, role, status, date applied, notes and link, moving through Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected and Ghosted. The application record behind an entry can include filled fields, generated answers, the résumé, cover letter and final submission result, varying by employer system. Add roles from elsewhere with **Add application** or **Import CSV** .


**Recruiter replies.** A dedicated Tsenta inbox receives application email. Tsenta classifies each message, for example as an interview, offer, rejection, assessment or verification email, links it to an application and moves the stage when the match is confident enough, and you can correct it by hand. You can also reply from your Tsenta address and forward a copy to an address you choose. Tsenta does not track replies from your personal Gmail or Outlook. Connecting either is optional and is used for passcodes on supported applications, not to read your mail, and Tsenta’s MCP server cannot read them.


**Through your assistant.** Tsenta’s MCP server connects your own assistant to your Tsenta account. It can read the status of every application Tsenta starts, move tracker entries, import up to 500 rows per request and summarize your Tsenta inbox: try “Did any recruiter reply to my applications this week?” One approval gives the assistant every available Tsenta tool, and whether it asks before each action depends on the assistant, not on Tsenta.


**Cost.** The tracker and reply monitoring are on every plan, and connecting an assistant is free. Your first 25 applications are free, once, with no card. In USD global pricing, Starter is $19 a month for 600 applications, Pro $39 for 1,500 and Power $99 for 4,500 per 30-day cycle ([pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) ).


### Tsenta as a Claude connector


In Claude, add` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` as a custom connector under **Customize** , then **Connectors** , sign in to Tsenta and approve, then set the apply and approve tools to **Always ask** if you see that option, or keep the chat in **Manual** mode. Free allows one custom connector, and Gmail and Notion are directory connectors, so Tsenta fits on Claude Free. Steps are on the[Claude connector page](https://tsenta.com/connectors/claude) .


### Tsenta as a ChatGPT app


On ChatGPT for the web, open **Plugins** , select **+** , then **Add custom MCP server** , enter` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` with OAuth, create it as a plugin and sign in to Tsenta.[OpenAI’s help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt) lists full MCP support, which moving tracker entries and applying need, on Business, Enterprise and Edu, and read and fetch only on Pro. On Business, only admins and owners can add a custom MCP server. Tsenta is not in ChatGPT’s plugin directory, and the full steps are on[tsenta.com/mcp](https://tsenta.com/mcp) .


### OpenClaw skill, Grok Bot plugin, Meta Muse or Instinct connector: can Tsenta connect?


Tsenta publishes setup only for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex, and has no guide for these four yet:


- **OpenClaw:** Tsenta connects as an MCP server rather than a skill. OpenClaw’s docs describe saving a remote server with the streamable-http transport and OAuth, as for Notion above, then running` openclaw mcp login` . Use Tsenta’s server address there.
- **Grok Bot:** possibly. Its docs say you can add a **Remote HTTPS** custom connector by server address in the desktop app, or ask Grok Bot to add an MCP server by its address. Use Tsenta’s server address and sign in if asked.
- **Meta Muse:** not as a documented setup yet. Muse can create custom connectors, but Meta’s public pages do not describe adding a remote MCP server by its address. If your Muse account supports custom remote MCP servers, give it Tsenta’s server address and sign in with OAuth.
- **Instinct:** not as a documented setup yet. Its public site does not describe custom connectors or MCP servers. If your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers, add Tsenta’s server address and sign in with OAuth.


The[Help Center guide](https://help.tsenta.com/connect-claude-chatgpt-mcp) covers privacy, disconnecting and troubleshooting.


## Do-it-yourself tracker vs Tsenta’s tracker


Do it yourself: assistant plus Gmail and Notion, Sheets or Airtable Tsenta’s tracker


**Who adds a row** Your assistant, when you run the prompt or on a schedule Tsenta, for each application it submits; you or your assistant for the rest


**Recruiter replies** Read from your Gmail, or Outlook in Muse, and proposed as a change Classified in your Tsenta inbox; the stage moves when the match is confident


**Applications you sent yourself** Covered, because their replies are in your Gmail Added by hand, by CSV or through your assistant; replies stay in your own inbox


**Sends applications** No Yes, on supported company career sites


**Where it works** Claude and ChatGPT with all four apps; Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct with fewer; OpenClaw with setup Tsenta’s web dashboard; Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex through the MCP server


**Cost** $0 on Claude Free with Notion Free; Claude’s scheduled tasks need a paid plan Tracker on every plan; 25 applications free, then from $19 a month for 600


**What can go wrong** Misread emails, duplicate rows, unreviewed writes if approvals are off Misclassified replies; one approval grants every Tsenta tool


The do-it-yourself setup wins on cost, sees replies to every application in your Gmail and lets you design every column. Tsenta wins when it is the one applying: an entry does not depend on a confirmation email arriving, and the application record can include what was sent, depending on the employer system. You can run both in one assistant: connect Gmail and Tsenta, and ask it to move the matching Tsenta entry when a reply lands in Gmail.


## Other trackers that work with AI assistants


[Simplify’s MCP server](https://help.simplify.jobs/articles/8107058-use-simplify-in-claude-chatgpt-and-codex-mcp) , published November 20, 2026, lets Claude, ChatGPT or Codex update its free Job Tracker and submit Autopilot applications after you say yes, and it needs Simplify+ at $39.99 a month. Simplify’s free Job Tracker also[connects Gmail directly](https://help.simplify.jobs/articles/5623502-whats-included-in-simplify-features-and-pricing) and suggests status updates from matched emails.[Himalayas’ MCP server](https://himalayas.app/mcp) adds a six-stage tracker with a free account, for remote roles only, and returns the application link rather than submitting.


[Teal](https://www.tealhq.com/pricing) tracks unlimited jobs free, and Teal+ costs $29 every 30 days.[Huntr](https://huntr.co/pricing) tracks up to 100 jobs free, and Pro costs $40 a month.[Careerflow](https://www.careerflow.ai/) ’s free plan has a limited tracker, and Premium costs $23.99 a month. We found no assistant integration for any of the three. Prices are as of November 20, 2026. Compare them in[Tsenta vs Teal](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-teal) ,[Tsenta vs Huntr](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-huntr) and our[free tracker roundup](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-free-job-application-tracker-apps-2026) .


## Which setup to choose


- **Free:** Claude Free with Gmail and Notion or Google Sheets, running the prompt by hand each week.
- **ChatGPT Plus or Pro:** Gmail plus Google Drive or Airtable, with a task on each new Gmail message.
- **Muse, Grok Bot or Instinct:** Gmail with Notion or a Google Sheet, on a recurring task, routine or weekly text.
- **OpenClaw:** the local tracker skill, or Notion’s server for a shared view.
- **One agent for applying and the log:** Tsenta, starting with 25 free applications.


Before tracking come applying and tailoring: read[how AI agents apply to jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-ai-agents-apply-to-jobs-2026) ,[tailoring your résumé through an assistant](https://tsenta.com/blog/ai-assistant-connectors-tailor-resume-2026) and[Meta Muse vs Grok Bot vs Instinct](https://tsenta.com/blog/meta-muse-vs-grok-bot-vs-instinct-job-search) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best Claude connectors for tracking job applications?


The best Claude connectors for tracking job applications are Gmail for confirmations and recruiter replies, and Notion, Google Sheets or Airtable for the tracker itself. Gmail, Notion and Airtable are verified listings in Anthropic’s directory, and Claude’s Google Sheets connector edits a sheet live beside the chat. For an agent that also applies and logs each application itself, add Tsenta’s MCP server as a custom connector.


### What are the best ChatGPT apps for tracking job applications?


The best ChatGPT apps for tracking job applications are Gmail, Notion, Airtable and Google Drive, which covers Google Sheets, all in ChatGPT’s plugin directory. Connect Gmail and one tracker app and ask ChatGPT to update the tracker from recent email. On Plus and Pro, a task can run each time a new Gmail message arrives.


### What are the best Muse connectors for tracking job applications?


The best Meta Muse connectors for tracking job applications are Gmail or Outlook for recruiter email and Notion for the tracker, all named on Meta’s own pages. Muse can also build a tracker as a Space and run it as a recurring task. Meta does not name Google Sheets or Airtable connectors, and Tsenta has no documented Muse setup yet.


### What are the best Grok Bot plugins for tracking job applications?


The best Grok Bot plugins for tracking job applications are the Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Drive and Notion apps in Grok Bot’s docs, run on a schedule as a routine. New subscribers get Grok Bot with The X Subscription’s Premium plan, $30 a month as of November 20, 2026, or higher. Tsenta can possibly be added as a custom connector, but Tsenta has no Grok Bot guide yet.


### What are the best Instinct connectors for tracking job applications?


Instinct’s only publicly named connection is Google Workspace, so the closest fit for tracking job applications with Instinct is Gmail plus a Google Sheet, which its August 2026 privacy policy listed. Instinct’s public pages do not describe Notion, Airtable, custom connectors or MCP servers, so Tsenta has no documented Instinct setup.


### What are the best OpenClaw skills for tracking job applications?


For tracking job applications in OpenClaw, use a tracker skill from ClawHub such as Job Hunt Tracker, which keeps your applications in local files, or connect Notion’s or Airtable’s hosted MCP server yourself. OpenClaw’s documented Gmail trigger uses Pub/Sub and needs Google Cloud setup. Tsenta connects to OpenClaw as an MCP server rather than a skill and has no OpenClaw guide yet.


### Can Claude connectors track job applications in Notion from Gmail?


Yes, Claude can track job applications in Notion from Gmail when both connectors are on. Ask it to search Gmail for confirmations and recruiter replies, match each one to a row in your Notion database and propose status changes for your approval. On paid plans, a scheduled task can run the same check every weekday.


### What are the best job application tracking tools with Gmail, Google Sheets, Notion and Airtable integrations in 2026?


In 2026, Claude and ChatGPT have the widest Gmail, Google Sheets, Notion and Airtable integrations for tracking job applications, because Anthropic and OpenAI each document connectors that reach all four. Simplify’s free Job Tracker connects Gmail itself and suggests status updates. Teal’s free plan tracks unlimited jobs and Huntr’s tracks up to 100, with no assistant integration we could find. Tsenta’s tracker imports a spreadsheet and fills itself as Tsenta applies.


### Is there a ChatGPT app that works as a job application tracker in 2026?


Yes, in 2026 ChatGPT works as a job application tracker through its Gmail, Google Drive, Notion and Airtable apps, or through OpenAI’s Track job applications use case in the ChatGPT desktop app, which builds a tracker spreadsheet from your files. Neither sends applications. Tsenta’s MCP server, added as a custom plugin on ChatGPT for the web, gives ChatGPT the tracker Tsenta fills as it applies, with full access on Business, Enterprise or Edu and read only on Pro.


### Does Tsenta read my Gmail to track recruiter replies?


No, Tsenta does not read your personal Gmail or Outlook to track recruiter replies. A dedicated Tsenta inbox receives application email, and Tsenta classifies those messages, links them to an application and moves its tracker stage when the match is confident enough. Connecting your own Gmail or Outlook is optional and is used for passcodes on supported applications, not to read your mail. Replies to applications you sent yourself stay in your own inbox.


### Can Tsenta track applications I sent outside Tsenta?


Yes, Tsenta’s tracker takes applications you sent elsewhere. Add one with Add application, bring in a spreadsheet with Import CSV or ask a connected assistant to import up to 500 rows at a time. Changing a stage never submits or cancels an employer application.
